2	
3	**Run:** `repo-battery-flight1`. **This is the run's ONLY leg.** It owns the entire delivery.
4	**Tree:** aion at rig commit `856b2a863`, base = landed main `cdde313b3`.
5	**Plan:** `.fleet/plan.md` (read it; this brief is self-contained but the plan carries the full
6	citation ledger and the measurements).
7	**Gate entry:** `.fleet/gate-entry.sh` — already committed, **not yours to edit**.
8	**Your report:** `.fleet/reports/build.md` (create it; `.fleet/reports/capture.md` is a prior run's).
9	
10	The brief's slices 1, 2 and 3 are **three sequential PHASES of this one leg**, in that order.
11	They are never parallel work items: **the proofs of phase 3 consume the workflow that phases 1 and
12	2 build.** Do not start phase 3 before phase 2 lands.

14	---
15	
16	## 0. Read this first — four facts that will save you a day
17	
18	1. **The design paper `docs/design/gate-battery-workflow-v2-20260818.md` is NOT in this repo**, at
19	   this tree or on any ref. Checked. `.fleet/BRIEF.md` rev 3 is the operative authority here, and it
20	   quotes or states every load-bearing section inline. **Do not invent a §-reading.** If a question
21	   turns on paper text the brief does not quote, it goes to **Artemis** (rulings ledger item 2 —
22	   she answers inside the hour, without reopening the grill), never to a guess.
23	2. **You may start no server and no listener.** No network services, no databases, no touching the
24	   live estate. See §6 for exactly which proofs that costs you and what you owe instead.
25	3. **Everything cited in this brief was re-verified at THIS tree**, because the brief was written
26	   against `c7fa6adba`. The same rule binds you: re-read any line before you lean on it.
27	4. **Vocabulary is binding: witness / record / attest. NEVER seal, NEVER pin.** Everywhere a
28	   recorded sha is described — in both documents, in the receipt's field docs, in the README, in
29	   your report. A seal REFUSES on mismatch; this **records** the sha256 and proceeds — it tells you
30	   afterwards which bytes ran. It *cannot* be a seal: the instrument lives inside the tree it
31	   measures, so there is no sha the operator can pin the subject repo against that the subject repo
32	   cannot also change. Pinning an expected sha in the operator's document is the two-lists problem
33	   wearing a different hat. (`gate_worker.awl:1-6` and `investigate_worker.awl:13` say "sealed" —
34	   pre-existing text, not yours to edit and not your precedent.)

38	## 1. What you are building
39	
40	New folder `workflows/repo-battery/`:
41	
42	| Path | What |
43	|---|---|
44	| `repo_battery.awl` | the workflow document — **ruled name `repo_battery`** |
45	| `repo_battery_worker.awl` | the worker document — **ruled queue `lane_repo_battery`** |
46	| `bin/*.sh` | the operation scripts |
47	| `README.md` | inputs, how to run, what a green does not prove |
48	| `proofs/` | fixtures, builder, harness, receipts |
49	
50	**Flow:** `admit` → `provision` → `precheck` → `battery` → `verify` → `receipt` → `teardown`.
51	
52	**FORBIDDEN — no edit, in any phase, for any reason:**
53	`workflows/gate/gate.awl`, `workflows/gates/gates.awl`, `workflows/gates/repo_gates.awl`.
54	Wave-1's closed leg vocabulary stays closed; v1 stays in service. F3 parallel-run
55	(`workflows/gates/README.md:300-311`) is the cut-over instrument, per repo, in a later lane.
56	
57	**The workflow INVOKES the repo's committed scripts. It never reimplements them.**
58	`scripts/battery.sh` and `scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh` are the instruments. §10.5's whole
59	indictment of the previous cut was: *"declared-versus-run is already enforced as a refusal — this
60	workflow simply never invoked it."* You are the invocation. You hold no leg list.

64	## 2. The substrate, measured at this tree — do not re-derive it
65	
66	**S1 — `scripts/battery.sh`'s source closure is exactly four files.**
67	`battery.sh:66` sources `scripts/gates/lib.sh`; `lib.sh:243` sources
68	`scripts/battery-costly-announcements.sh`; the estate-root walk (`battery.sh:98-104`) is conditional
69	and finds nothing at this venue. Both `battery.sh:56` and `verify-declaration.sh:48` derive
70	`REPO_ROOT` from `BASH_SOURCE` — **script location, not git.** So a tree holding
71	`scripts/battery.sh`, `scripts/gates/lib.sh`, `scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh`,
72	`scripts/battery-costly-announcements.sh` plus a `gates.json` is a runnable subject repo.
73	**Measured: it is.** A two-leg fixture built that way ran green (battery rc 0,
74	`EXECUTED_LEGS fixture:reads-tree fixture:true`) and verify-declaration returned
75	`VERDICT: exact match`, rc 0.
76	
77	**S2 — `scripts/gates/lib.sh` is bash and must NEVER run under `sh`.**
78	`lib.sh:1` is `#!/usr/bin/env bash`; `lib.sh:91` uses process substitution
79	(`done < <(type -ap python3 2>/dev/null)`). Measured: `sh ./scripts/battery.sh` → **rc 2**, dying at
80	`battery.sh: 56: Bad substitution` (`${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`) then
81	`battery.sh: 66: .: cannot open //scripts/gates/lib.sh`. It never reaches the declaration read and
82	emits no `EXECUTED_LEGS`. **Rule: invoke these scripts so their bash shebang is honoured, or invoke
83	them as `bash <script>` explicitly. Never `sh <script>`.** Note that
84	`workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl:28` uses `sh <script>` — those are `#!/bin/sh`
85	scripts. Yours are not. Do not copy that half of the precedent.
86	
87	**S3 — a suppressed leg leaves the battery GREEN; only verify-declaration catches it.**
88	Measured: `AION_BATTERY_ONLY="fixture:true" ./scripts/battery.sh` → **rc 0**, `0 of 1 gates failed`.
89	The same log through `verify-declaration.sh` → **rc 1**,
90	`🔴 DECLARED BUT NOT EXECUTED — the population shrank: fixture:reads-tree`.
91	This is your `unproven` discriminator, already committed in the subject repo. Proof 3's instrument
92	exists; your job is to invoke it and route on it.
93	
94	**S4 — a dead selector and a real drift are INDISTINGUISHABLE at the instrument.**
95	Measured: `gates.json` with `"legs": []` → `verify-declaration.sh` exits **1**
96	("the declaration lists no legs"); a genuine declared-but-not-executed drift also exits **1**. Same
97	code, different worlds. **Therefore the discrimination MUST live in your census, as a typed refusal
98	naming the selector path — never inferred from an exit code.** This is R3, measured.
99	
100	**S5 — `gates.json` declares environment as NAMES ONLY, and exactly one leg does.**
101	24 legs; leg 23 `estate-guard` carries `"environment": ["ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT"]`; the other 23 carry
102	none. And: **no leg carries a literal absolute path.** `estate-guard`'s
103	`"$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/gates/hooks/check_must_be_claimed.sh"` is **variable-rooted, not
104	absolute**. A checker that reds it would red aion's own honest declaration on its first real run —
105	which is how a correct instrument gets switched off. See §5.4.
106	
107	**S6 — the venue.** `aion` at `/home/aion/.cargo/bin/aion`; `cargo`/`rustc` per
108	`rust-toolchain.toml` (`1.97.1`, rustfmt + clippy); `bash`, `git`, `python3`, `jq` present; `bun`
109	and `node` present at the **transient** path `/tmp/bun-node-0d9b296af/`; **`gleam` ABSENT**, **`uv`
110	ABSENT**; `tools/gates/lib/estate-root.sh` absent anywhere on the walk to `/`;
111	`ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT` unset; this tree is a plain clone, **not** a worktree.
112	**Consequence: aion's own 24-leg battery cannot go green here** (3 gleam legs + 2 python legs → 127
113	via `require_tool`, `lib.sh:40-52`; `estate-guard` → rc 3 by its own declared refusal). That is a
114	**venue fact, not a code verdict**, and it is not a defect to fix. Your positive control is a
115	purpose-built fixture, which is what the brief requires.
116	
117	---
118	
119	## 3. The AWL language surface — every construct below was prototyped and checks green
120	
121	Prototyped in `/tmp/awlproto` against `/home/aion/.cargo/bin/aion`. **Use these; they work.**
122	
123	- **L1 — per-field `///` docs are first-class.** `FieldDecl` carries `pub docs: Vec<DocLine>`
124	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/ast/document.rs:329-335`); the parser attaches them
125	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/parser/types.rs:188,235`) and names fields in its own diagnostic:
126	  "`///` doc lines attach to declarations (types, fields, actions, steps)"
127	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/parser/statements.rs:25`).
128	  **G2, R1 and R2 go in the receipt type's own FIELD docs — not in the `//!` header.**
129	- **L2 — an action may declare `timeout` with NO `retry` clause.** Checks green. And retry is
130	  declaration-owned: a call site "may pin `node` and `timeout` only — `retry` stays on the
131	  declaration" (`crates/aion-awl/src/checker/calls.rs:98-104`). **The no-retry law is expressed by
132	  omission and cannot be defeated at a call site.**
133	- **L3 — a typed refusal may route to SUCCESS.** `outcome undeclared: type Undeclared, route success`
134	  checks green and lowers to `Ok(UndeclaredOutcome(…))`.
135	- **L4 — string and empty-list literals are legal route arguments.**
136	  `route undeclared(verdict: "undeclared", …)` and `script_witnesses: []` both check green. AWL
137	  composes no strings at runtime, so the typed literal is a literal.
138	- **L5 — list-of-record inputs and fields check green:** `input waivers: [Waiver]`,
139	  `legs: [LegRecord]`, `script_witnesses: [ScriptWitness]`.
140	- **L6 — `sequence` can iterate an activity-bound list** (`sequence name in c.legs_declared`).
141	  Available. **You must not use it for the census** — see §5.3.
142	- **L7 — combinators are `filter`, `map`, `sort`, `count`, `any`, `all`**
143	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/ast/steps.rs:234-247`), and a comparison predicate is legal:
144	  `waivers |> any(.ruled_by == "") -> anonymous` checks green, as does
145	  `c.legs_declared |> count -> n` with `when n == 0`. **Proof 6's waiver refusal and R3's zero-leg
146	  refusal are both expressible in the workflow, at input, before anything is provisioned.**
147	- **L8 — the receipt's serialized field order IS its declaration order.** Measured with a
148	  deliberately non-alphabetical type: the emitter writes `receipt_to_json` as
149	  `json.object([#("zeta",…), #("alpha",…), #("mid_field",…)])`, declaration order. The beam
150	  sidecar's `required` array is likewise declaration order — the `properties` *object* is
151	  alphabetised, so **`required` is the order witness, not `properties`.** This is how R4 is checked.
152	- **L9 — `aion awl fmt` has NO `--check` mode** (its own help: "the printer is the single formatter,
153	  one rendering, so there is no `--check` mode"). It rewrites in place. **Do not run it.**
154	  `aion awl check` is the acceptance.
155	- **L10 — worker-document bodies admit no shell variables, so logic beyond one command lives in a
156	  script file.** The repo states it: `workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl:7-13`. This is the
157	  language constraint that grounds §5.2.
158	
159	**Working skeleton, checked green** (`ok: … (2 steps)`), as your starting shape:
160	
161	```awl
162	workflow probe_shape
163	  timeout 6h
164	  input subject_ref: String
165	  outcome reported:   type Receipt,    route success
166	  outcome undeclared: type Undeclared, route success
167	  outcome unmeasured: type Unmeasured, route failure
168	
169	type Receipt {
170	  /// The head commit of the provisioned tree, WITNESSED at provision.
171	  head_commit: String,
172	  /// VERDICT INVERSION: a red battery is a SUCCESSFUL measurement.
173	  verdict: String,
174	}
175	
176	worker battery_ops
177	  /// No retry clause at all — battery legs never retry.
178	  action provision(subject_ref: String) -> Probe
179	    timeout 30m
180	```
181	
182	---
183	
184	## 4. Phase 1 — the workflow: provision, invoke, receipt
185	
186	**P1.1** Create `workflows/repo-battery/`. New document pair. **No edit** to `gate.awl`,
187	`gates.awl`, `repo_gates.awl`.
188	
189	**P1.2** Names, ruled and not yours to vary: workflow `repo_battery`, queue `lane_repo_battery`.
190	The shape matches the existing `lane_gates` (`workflows/gates/worker/src/main.rs:32`).
191	
192	**P1.3 The flow.**
193	
194	- **`admit`** — input validation, **before anything is provisioned**. A waiver missing its author is
195	  refused here (L7). Provisions nothing, costs nothing.
196	- **`provision`** — clone/worktree the subject repo at the **caller-named ref** into a **RUN-OWNED
197	  tree** under the venue's workspace root — **never a person's checkout** (§9.5's measured reason).
198	  Refusals are data; a leftover destination **refuses** rather than being deleted —
199	  `workflows/investigate/bin/clone.sh:26` is the register, verbatim: *"a leftover tree from a
200	  collided dispatch, the dispatcher's to inspect"*.

201	- **`precheck`** — venue pre-checks **recorded, not assumed**. See §5.5.
202	- **`battery`** — ONE whole-cloth command: run **the tree's own** `scripts/battery.sh`,
203	  exit-zero-always, **rc + log path + contended flag as data** — the `gate_worker.awl:13-24` probe

205	- **`verify`** — run **the tree's own** `scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh` against the battery
206	  log. **Its refusal IS the scope instrument** (S3). Never reimplemented.
207	- **`receipt`** — the terminal typed report (§5).
208	- **`teardown`** — **run-owned tree only**, root-guarded, with the guard in the **same script that
209	  does the `rm`, never a separate command**: `workflows/investigate/bin/teardown.sh:3-6` states the
210	  law — *"Deletion inherits every adjective of its justification"* — and `:14-28` implements it.
211	  Teardown obligations are **surfaced, not assumed**, on every route that owns a tree.
212	
213	**P1.4 / P1.5 — invoke, never reimplement.** `scripts/battery.sh:42-45` is the reason, in its own
214	header: *"🔴 THE CURE IS SUBTRACTION, NOT A CHECKER. A drift-checker would be a third copy of the
215	same list."* `verify-declaration.sh:6-18` says the same of itself: it *"holds no list of its own"*.
216	Your workflow holds no list either.
217	
218	**P1.6 — never `sh <script>`** (S2).
219	
220	**P1.7 — exit-zero-always, refusal as typed data on every anticipated face.** `gate_worker.awl:13-16`
221	states why: *"a nonzero exit is a retryable-then-terminal activity failure and the workflow must
222	ROUTE on these faces."* Genuine breakage (unspawnable script, dead disk) may exit nonzero; a red
223	suite, a missing tree, an unreadable log may not.
224	
225	**P1.8 — no retry on battery legs; the workflow timeout is the one duration.** No per-leg retry
226	ladder anywhere.
227	
228	**P1.9 — no child workflows anywhere.** The cancellation contract abandons children. Every long leg
229	under **process-group containment**; a cancelled leg reports **CANCELLED MEASUREMENT**, never a
230	result.
231	
232	**P1.10 / P1.11** — run-owned tree; root-guarded teardown; obligations surfaced.
233	
234	**P1.12 — fmt is never a gate** (`gate.awl:40-42`, STANDING ORDER 9) — **and** aion's `gates.json`
235	declares `rust:fmt` (leg 0, `cargo fmt --all -- --check`). The workflow **runs what the repo
236	declares**: the repo's list is the contract. If the estate wants aion's fmt leg gone, that is a diff
237	to aion's `gates.json` under its own review, not a workflow opinion. **G4 is Vesper's to settle
238	separately — build neither around it nor waiting on it.** Do not add an fmt-suppression path;
239	Artemis's endorsement, not to be softened: *a suppressed leg is a second list one item long.*
240	
241	**P1.13 — manual start only.** No cadence, no CI trigger, no schedule
242	(`workflows/gates/README.md:290-293`).
243	
244	**P1.14 — the folder carries its own README**, and the `//!` header states what the workflow
245	measures **and what that does not prove** — `workflows/README.md:56-59`: *"In the `//!` header, not
246	only in the README. The document travels; the README does not."*
247	
248	---
249	
250	## 5. Phase 2 — the receipt attests its own scope, nothing wider
251	
252	### 5.1 The receipt's fields, in exactly this order
253	
254	**R4 is load-bearing NOW, at full strength.** L8 proves declaration order is serialization order, so
255	the order below **is** the wire order, every run:
256	
257	1. `subject_repo` · 2. `ref_requested` · 3. `head_commit` · 4. `tree_path` ·
258	5. `gates_json_sha256` · 6. `battery_sha256` · 7. `script_witnesses` (`[ScriptWitness]`, sorted by
259	`path`) · 8. `venue` · 9. `environment` (`[EnvRecord]`, declaration order per leg) ·
260	10. `legs_declared` · 11. `legs_executed` · 12. `legs` (`[LegRecord]`: name, rc, status) ·
261	13. `verify_verdict` · 14. `waivers` · 15. `verdict`.
262	
263	> **R4, verbatim and binding:** *this stable-shape-and-order requirement is LOAD-BEARING NOW, at full
264	> strength, even though the drift check that consumes it is out of scope: comparability cannot be
265	> retrofitted onto receipts already written, so this phase ships witnesses to the ordering discipline
266	> on the strength of a consumer that does not exist yet. **A builder must not read "drift check out
267	> of scope" as licence to drop the ordering.***
268	
269	`legs_executed` comes from the battery's own `EXECUTED_LEGS` line (`scripts/battery.sh:282`), which
270	`verify-declaration.sh:102-119` requires to appear **exactly once** in the log.
271	
272	### 5.2 Where the logic lives — RULED, do not re-open
273	
274	**The mechanical logic goes in committed scripts under `workflows/repo-battery/bin/`, invoked by the
275	worker document's bodies.** Not an SDK crate (Vesper: a crate brings a `Cargo.lock` that rots — she
276	measured sixteen out-of-workspace worker projects pinning beamr 0.6.1 through 0.18.2 while the root
277	moved to 0.19.3; a document has no lock to rot). Not 400-character single-quoted `sh -c` bodies
278	carrying python either.
279	
280	The reason is the language constraint at L10, stated in this repo:
281	`workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl:7-13`. `investigate_ops` is a live first-party workflow
282	built exactly this way. A committed script **is** reviewable text at a sha, and its sha256 is
283	**witnessed** into the receipt. This is named in `.fleet/plan.md` §4.2 as a planner's call, for the
284	landing desk to review — do not quietly change it either way.
285	
286	### 5.3 ONE census site — this is R3's foundation
287	
288	The provisioned tree's `gates.json` is read **once**, in **one** script, at **one** site:
289	`bin/census-declaration.sh`. **Do not** smear the selector across a worker body, a workflow pipe
290	chain and a step guard, and **do not** use `sequence` to iterate `legs_declared` even though L6
291	proves you could.
292	
293	The reason is proof 8b: the selector-perturbation arm needs a **single nameable selector site with a
294	`file:line` address** to aim at. Three sites is three places to be right and no address to break.
295	And the battery does not need iteration: `scripts/battery.sh:226-239` runs the whole declared list
296	itself and reports per-leg rc in its manifest (`:264-274`).
297	
298	### 5.4 The absolute-path admission rule, stated precisely
299	
300	Refuse **at admission** a declared leg whose **command** contains a **literal absolute path** — a `/`
301	beginning a path token, not preceded by a word character or `$`. Keyed on the **PATH INSIDE THE
302	COMMAND, never the leg's name** (§10.2: ten of thirteen estate gate lists carry such a leg under
303	differing names).
304	
305	**A variable-rooted path is NOT an absolute path.** `"$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/…"` is aion's own
306	leg 23 and is handled by the environment pre-check (§5.5), not by this rule. S5 measured this: a rule
307	that reds it would red aion's honest declaration on its first real run.
308	
309	### 5.5 Venue pre-checks — recorded, not assumed
310	
311	- The repo's `rust-toolchain.toml` pin vs the venue's matching toolchain, **with targets**.
312	- **PATH order** — rustup shim first.
313	- **Hydration**: the fresh-tree step the repo's own docs name (for aion:
314	  `bun install --frozen-lockfile`) — untracked `node_modules` otherwise reads as **five red legs that
315	  look like code failures**. **G5, ruled: this is a declared rc-3-style refusal on aion's side, NEVER
316	  an auto-install. An instrument must not mutate the venue it measures.**
317	- **Environment, at Artemis's strength — NOT "confirmed set".** For each name in a leg's declared
318	  `environment` block: **confirm and record the VALUE** for non-secret variables; **presence plus a
319	  digest** for anything secret-shaped. The reason is the correction's own: *a variable set to a
320	  DIFFERENT value than the leg's scope assumes is the silent scope change itself, and it passes a
321	  set-check.* The effective environment is **recorded in the receipt beside the frozen HEAD**.
322	  Reason to carry into the field docs: a gate's scope is set by its environment as much as by its
323	  declaration; the standing true receipt for the class is the estate's runtime env-gated tests — a
324	  leg whose tests read a `*_TEST_URL`-style variable and skip when unset measures a **different
325	  scope** with and without it, while reporting the same green. Receipts whose environments do not
326	  travel with their verdicts are not comparable: pass counts compare verdicts, not what was asked.
327	
328	### 5.6 The four sentences that MUST appear in the receipt type's own FIELD docs
329	
330	Not in the `//!` header. In the **field documentation** (L1) — because the reader who tidies this
331	away will be holding the field docs, not the design paper. These are machine-readable in the beam
332	sidecar as JSON-Schema `description` strings, and §7.4 asserts them there.
333	
334	- **G2 — verdict inversion, on `verdict`, with its reason.** A red gate routes to workflow
335	  **SUCCESS**; `Failed` is reserved for **could-not-measure**; only `unproven` routes to failure.
336	  The reason, stated: **the status answers "did I measure?", the receipt answers "what did I
337	  measure?"** — because a red gate reporting SUCCESS is exactly the shape a later reader tidies away.
338	- **R1 — the authority sentence, on the fields that name a ref and a venue.** "No new trust" is true
339	  of the CODE and false of the VENUE: pre-existing, the self-gating hazard sat inside aion's own CI
340	  under aion's authority; this workflow moves it to a fleet venue that may hold credentials, network
341	  reach, and neighbours. State it plainly, in these words:
342	  **A BATTERY RUNS WITH THE VENUE'S AUTHORITY, AND NAMING A REF IS THEREFORE AN AUTHORITY-BEARING
343	  ACT.**
344	- **R2 — `undeclared`'s explicit status, in the same field docs.** Workflow status **SUCCESS** — the
345	  workflow measured the tree and found no contract; a **determinate census result**, not a
346	  could-not-measure. Receipt verdict is the typed literal **`undeclared`**, which consumers **MUST**
347	  treat as **not-a-verdict**: never green, never red, never pass-by-omission. State the reason: *a
348	  refusal with no assigned status resolves to the runtime's default, and a repo with no `gates.json`

399	  seam the server's `POST /awl/deploy` path uses" (its own `--help`) and writes `<out>.beam.json`

117	  `POST /awl/deploy` path uses" (its own `--help`) and writes a `<out>.beam.json` sidecar carrying
118	  the derived `output_schema`. Measured on a prototype: **per-field `///` docs travel into that
119	  sidecar as JSON-Schema `description` strings**, and the `required` array is in **declaration
120	  order**. So G2/R1/R2's field docs and R4's field order are *machine-assertable offline*.
121	
122	What genuinely needs the engine is the **routing and cancellation** half: that a red battery lands on
123	a SUCCESS route, that `undeclared` lands on a SUCCESS route, that a mid-battery cancel yields
124	CANCELLED MEASUREMENT. Two of those three are also assertable *structurally* offline, from the
125	emitted Gleam, which lowers a success route to `Ok(<Outcome>(…))` and a failure route to
126	`Error(awl_error.AwlOutcomeFailure(…))` (measured on a prototype). A structural assertion is weaker
127	than an execution and is labelled as such wherever it is used — it is never called a receipt.
128	
129	Full per-proof allocation is the matrix in §6.
130	
131	---
132	
133	## 2. Language findings — every construct prototyped against the real binary
134	
135	Prototyped in `/tmp/awlproto` with `/home/aion/.cargo/bin/aion`, all checking green. These are
136	facts, not preferences, and the leg brief prescribes only constructs that appear here.
137	
138	- **L1 — per-field `///` docs are first-class AWL.** `FieldDecl` carries `pub docs: Vec<DocLine>`
139	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/ast/document.rs:329-335`); the parser attaches them
140	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/parser/types.rs:188,235`) and names fields explicitly in its own diagnostic:
141	  "`///` doc lines attach to declarations (types, fields, actions, steps)"
142	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/parser/statements.rs:25`). **G2, R1 and R2 can therefore be satisfied
143	  literally, in the receipt type's own field documentation, as required — not in a header comment.**
144	- **L2 — an action may declare `timeout` with NO `retry` clause.** Checks green. Retry is
145	  declaration-owned, and a call site "may pin `node` and `timeout` only — `retry` stays on the
146	  declaration" (`crates/aion-awl/src/checker/calls.rs:98-104`). **The no-retry law is expressible by
147	  omission, and is not defeasible at a call site.**
148	- **L3 — a typed refusal may route to SUCCESS.** `outcome undeclared: type Undeclared, route success`
149	  checks green, and lowers to `Ok(UndeclaredOutcome(…))`. **R2 is directly expressible.**
150	- **L4 — string and empty-list literals are legal route arguments.** `route undeclared(verdict:
151	  "undeclared", …)` and `script_witnesses: []` both check green. **The typed not-a-verdict literal
152	  needs no runtime composition** (AWL composes no strings at runtime).
153	- **L5 — list-of-record inputs and list-of-record fields check green.** `input waivers: [Waiver]`,
154	  `legs: [LegRecord]`, `script_witnesses: [ScriptWitness]`.
155	- **L6 — `sequence` iterates an ACTIVITY-BOUND list, not only an input.** `sequence name in
156	  c.legs_declared` where `c` is an activity result checks green (5 steps). Available, but §4.3 rules
157	  it *out* for the census on purpose.
158	- **L7 — the combinator vocabulary is `filter`, `map`, `sort`, `count`, `any`, `all`**
159	  (`crates/aion-awl/src/ast/steps.rs:234-247`; `crates/aion-awl/src/checker/stages.rs:1-3`), and a
160	  comparison predicate is legal in one: `waivers |> any(.ruled_by == "") -> anonymous` checks green,
161	  as does `c.legs_declared |> count -> n` with `when n == 0`. **Proof 6's waiver refusal and R3's
162	  zero-leg refusal are both expressible in the workflow, at input, before anything is provisioned.**
163	- **L8 — the receipt's serialized field order IS its declaration order.** The emitter writes
164	  `receipt_to_json` as `json.object([#("zeta", …), #("alpha", …), #("mid_field", …)])` in
165	  declaration order, measured with a deliberately non-alphabetical type. The beam sidecar's
166	  `required` array is likewise in declaration order (the `properties` *object* is alphabetised, so
167	  `required` is the order witness, not `properties`). **R4 is satisfied by declaring the fields in
168	  the ruled order, and it is mechanically checkable.**
169	- **L9 — `aion awl fmt` has no `--check` mode.** Its own help says so: "the printer is the single
170	  formatter, one rendering, so there is no `--check` mode." It rewrites in place. **It must not be
171	  run as an acceptance step; `aion awl check` is the acceptance.**
172	- **L10 — worker-document bodies admit no shell variables, so logic beyond one command lives in a
173	  script file.** Not a preference — the stated language constraint and the standing first-party
174	  precedent: `workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl:7-13`, whose actions are
175	  `run json "sh /home/aion/fleet/bin/<op>.sh $params"` (`:28`), with the scripts' source of truth in
176	  that folder's `bin/`. See §4.2 for the ruling this grounds.
177	
178	---
179	
180	## 3. The substrate, measured — five things the builder must not re-derive
181	
182	Measured here at this tree, with real runs, in `/tmp/fixproof`.
183	
184	**S1 — the source closure of `scripts/battery.sh` is exactly four files.** `battery.sh:66` sources
185	`scripts/gates/lib.sh`; `lib.sh:243` sources `scripts/battery-costly-announcements.sh`; the
186	estate-root walk (`battery.sh:98-104`) is conditional and finds nothing here. Both `battery.sh:56`
187	and `verify-declaration.sh:48` derive `REPO_ROOT` from `BASH_SOURCE` — **script location, not git**.
188	So the closure is `scripts/battery.sh`, `scripts/gates/lib.sh`, `scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh`,
189	`scripts/battery-costly-announcements.sh`, and a tree holding those four plus a `gates.json` is a
190	runnable subject repo. **Measured: it is.** A two-leg fixture built exactly that way ran green
191	(battery rc 0, `EXECUTED_LEGS fixture:reads-tree fixture:true`) and verify-declaration returned
192	`VERDICT: exact match`, rc 0.
193	
194	**S2 — the `sh` hazard is real, loud, and early.** `sh ./scripts/battery.sh` → **rc 2**, dying at
195	`battery.sh: 56: Bad substitution` (`${BASH_SOURCE[0]}`) and then
196	`battery.sh: 66: .: cannot open //scripts/gates/lib.sh`. It never reaches the declaration read and
197	emits no `EXECUTED_LEGS`. The brief's rule is confirmed with a file and a line: **invoke these
198	scripts so their bash shebang is honoured, or invoke them as `bash <script>` — never `sh <script>`.**
199	
200	**S3 — a suppressed leg leaves the battery GREEN and only verify-declaration catches it.** Measured:
201	`AION_BATTERY_ONLY="fixture:true" ./scripts/battery.sh` → **rc 0**, `0 of 1 gates failed`; the same
202	log through `verify-declaration.sh` → **rc 1**, `🔴 DECLARED BUT NOT EXECUTED — the population
203	shrank: fixture:reads-tree`. This is the `unproven` discriminator, and it is why §10.5's indictment
204	bites: *the battery's own exit code cannot see this.* Proof 3 has its instrument, already committed
205	in the subject repo, and the workflow's job is to **invoke** it.
206	
207	**S4 — a dead selector and a real drift are INDISTINGUISHABLE at the instrument.** Measured: a
208	`gates.json` with `"legs": []` run through `verify-declaration.sh` exits **1** with "the declaration
209	lists no legs"; a genuine declared-but-not-executed drift also exits **1**. Same code, different
210	worlds. This is R3's collision, measured at this tree rather than argued — and it fixes *where* the
211	discrimination must live: **in the workflow's own census, as a typed refusal naming the selector
212	path, never inferred from an exit code.**
213	
214	**S5 — `gates.json` declares environment as NAMES ONLY, and exactly one leg does.** Leg 23
215	`estate-guard` carries `"environment": ["ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT"]`; the other 23 carry none. So
216	Artemis's refinement — *confirm and record the VALUE, not merely that it is set* — is satisfiable:
217	the name comes from the declaration, the value from the environment about to fire. Also measured:
218	**no leg in aion's `gates.json` carries a literal absolute path.** `estate-guard`'s
219	`"$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/gates/hooks/check_must_be_claimed.sh"` is **variable-rooted, not
220	absolute**, and a checker that reds it would red aion's own honest declaration. §4.5 states the rule

1	//! investigate — one threshold-crossing issue, investigated by an agent on a
2	//! remote worker box, filed back to the tracker as a typed report — on the
3	//! engine's own durability, with the pipeline proven against a known answer
4	//! before any real judgement is spent, and the tree torn down on every route
5	//! that owns one.
6	//!
7	//! This is the issue-investigation workflow of the ratified design
8	//! (`docs/design/issue-investigation-workflow-20260818.md` in the estate docs
9	//! repo). Its architecture is deliberately stock: the mechanical legs (clone,
10	//! report read-back, filing, teardown) are served by `aion worker awl` from
11	//! this folder's worker document, and the agent seam is served by
12	//! `aion worker agent` from THIS document's `investigator` harness section —
13	//! no bespoke crate. The estate server orchestrates; the workers live on the
14	//! investigation box; every run is visible in the operator's console.
15	//!
16	//! THE TREE IS THE BLACKBOARD, exactly as fleet_dev records: AWL composes no
17	//! strings at runtime, so every mechanical action takes (workspace_root,
18	//! workflow_id) and derives its own paths from them by one shared rule —
19	//! the run's tree is `<workspace_root>/<workflow_id>/repo`, the agent's
20	//! deliverable is `<tree>/.investigation/report.json` — and the
21	//! investigator's prompt is an ADDRESS the dispatcher builds, naming that
22	//! report path as the deliverable. The report the workflow returns is READ
23	//! BACK FROM THE TREE and parsed into the declared type: a reply that
24	//! claimed a report the tree does not carry routes to `unreported`, because
25	//! a reply is a claim and the tree is the fact.
26	//!
27	//! CONTROL-FIRST, against the CLONED tree: before the investigator sees the
28	//! issue, the probe action asks a question whose answer the dispatcher
29	//! already knows — quote a literal at a known path in the clone — and the
30	//! whole run refuses to `unmeasured` on any other reply. An investigator
31	//! that cannot read the tree returns confident verdicts indistinguishable
32	//! from real ones; the control is the only thing that can tell.
33	//!
34	//! VERDICT IS DATA, NEVER WORKFLOW FAILURE (aion#58, from birth): a filed
35	//! investigation completes on route `filed` whatever its verdict says —
36	//! `NotReproduced` is a successful investigation, not a failed workflow.
37	//! The failure routes are reserved for could-not-measure faces, each named:
38	//! `unsupported_tracker` (github-only v1, refused BY NAME — a skipped issue
39	//! is indistinguishable from a swept-and-clean issue), `unprovisioned` (the
40	//! clone refused; a leftover tree is a fact to surface, never to delete in
41	//! passing), `unmeasured` (control mismatch), `unanswered` (the agent's stop
42	//! reason was not end_turn), `unreported` (report absent or unparseable),
43	//! `unfiled` (the tracker write failed — the typed report SURVIVES in the
44	//! payload; evidence is never lost to a tracker hiccup).
45	//!
46	//! THE WORKFLOW NEVER CLOSES, LABELS-AS-RESOLVED, OR ASSIGNS the issue. Its
47	//! terminal is `filed`; the lead's review is a human step outside the run.
48	//!
49	//! STATED GAPS, not latent ones: (1) the design's deterministic-id
50	//! idempotency clause (`investigate/<repo>/<issue>/<threshold>`) is not
51	//! expressible on today's start surface — `aion start` mints the id and
52	//! takes only a display `--name`; dispatchers carry the deterministic string
53	//! as the name until the start surface takes an id. (2) the harness
54	//! `--workspace-root` argument is a static document value, so this document
55	//! is authored PER DEPLOYMENT (this one: the aion-workflows box,
56	//! `/home/aion/fleet/runs`); the `workspace_root` input must name the same
57	//! root, and the worker document's scripts refuse teardown outside it.
58	//! (3) node pinning is by queue occupancy in v1 — one box serves both
59	//! queues; the `node` input is carried as record, not enforcement.
60	//!
61	//! WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: a filed report is one model's unverified
62	//! reading of the tree, control-proven but not fact-checked. Every citation
63	//! must be read by hand before anything acts on it — the filed comment says
64	//! exactly that, where the reader is.
65	workflow investigate
66	  timeout 4h
67	  input issue: IssueRef
68	  input threshold: String
69	  input node_label: String
70	  input repo_url: String
71	  input workspace_root: String
72	  input control_prompt: String
73	  input control_expect: String
74	  input investigate_prompt: String
75	  outcome filed:               type Filed,              route success
76	  outcome unsupported_tracker: type UnsupportedTracker, route failure
77	  outcome unprovisioned:       type CloneRefused,       route failure
78	  outcome unmeasured:          type Refused,            route failure
79	  outcome unanswered:          type Unanswered,         route failure
80	  outcome unreported:          type Unreported,         route failure
81	  outcome unfiled:             type Unfiled,            route failure
82	
83	/// The issue under investigation. `tracker` names the seam: v1 serves
84	/// `github` and refuses anything else by name. `number` is a string because
85	/// it is an argument to the tracker's CLI, never arithmetic.
86	type IssueRef { tracker: String, repo: String, number: String, title: String }
87	
88	/// The canonical agent-outcome record every dispatch of an agent seam
89	/// returns: accumulated `text`, the last answer alone as `final_message`,
90	/// the canonical `stop_reason`, and the `session_id` audit handle.
91	type Reply { text: String, final_message: String, stop_reason: String, session_id: String }
92	
93	/// The clone's answer, exit-zero always: a refusal is data with its reason
94	/// named, because a nonzero exit would be a retryable-then-terminal activity
95	/// failure and a leftover tree must route, not crash. `head_commit` pins
96	/// what tree the evidence is about; `clone_bytes` feeds the census audit.
97	type CloneProbe { ok: Bool, refusal: String, path: String, head_commit: String, clone_bytes: Int }
98	
99	/// The read-back's answer: the report parsed into the declared type when the
100	/// tree carries one, and the parse failure verbatim when it does not.
101	/// `report` is optional rather than empty-but-present — "nothing went wrong"
102	/// and "nobody wrote it" must not arrive as the same value.
103	type ReportProbe { parse_error: String, report: InvestigationReport? }
104	
105	/// One piece of evidence: file:line or it isn't evidence.
106	type Evidence { path: String, line: Int, excerpt: String }
107	
108	/// The investigator's deliverable, authored INTO THE TREE and read back
109	/// typed. These are the agent-authored fields only: `session_id` and the
110	/// control proof are workflow-known facts the FILING carries beside the
111	/// report, because the session cannot know its own audit handle.
112	type InvestigationReport {
113	  schema_version: String,
114	  issue: String,
115	  repo: String,
116	  head_commit: String,
117	  verdict: Verdict,
118	  summary: String,
119	  evidence: [Evidence],
120	  repro: String?,
121	  proposed_fix: String?,
122	  confidence: String,
123	}
124	
125	/// No free-text verdicts. `NotReproduced` says "I could not make it happen
126	/// at head_commit"; `AlreadyFixed` says "here is the commit that closed it"
127	/// and requires an evidence entry naming that commit.
128	type Verdict = Reproduced | NotReproduced | AlreadyFixed | NeedsInfo | WrongRepo
129	
130	/// The tracker write's answer, exit-zero always for the same reason as the
131	/// clone's: a red filing routes `unfiled` with the report intact.
132	type FilingProbe { ok: Bool, exit_code: Int, stderr: String, url: String }
133	
134	/// The teardown's answer. A refusal (path outside the run root, tree
135	/// already gone) is data; the census sweeper owns whatever a refusal
136	/// leaves behind.
137	type TeardownProbe { ok: Bool, removed: String, refusal: String }
138	
139	/// A filed investigation: the typed report, where it landed, the audit
140	/// handle, the control's own evidence, and whether the tree came down.
141	type Filed {
142	  report: InvestigationReport,
143	  filing_url: String,
144	  session_id: String,
145	  control_reply: String,
146	  teardown_ok: Bool,
147	}
148	
149	/// v1 is github-only and any other tracker is refused BY NAME — never
150	/// silently skipped, never best-effort.
151	type UnsupportedTracker { tracker: String, reason: String }
152	
153	/// The clone refused — including a leftover tree from a collided id, which
154	/// is the dispatcher's to inspect, never a script's to delete.
155	type CloneRefused { refusal: String, node: String }
156	
157	/// An investigation that did not investigate, said out loud: the control's
158	/// expected and actual replies travel with the refusal.
159	type Refused { control_expect: String, control_reply: String, reason: String, teardown_ok: Bool }
160	
161	/// The agent seam ended without a completed answer; the whole agent record's
162	/// identifying fields travel for the audit.
163	type Unanswered { stop_reason: String, session_id: String, final_message: String, teardown_ok: Bool }
164	
165	/// The agent answered but the tree carries no parseable report — the reply
166	/// was a claim the tree does not back.
167	type Unreported { parse_error: String, session_id: String, final_message: String, teardown_ok: Bool }
168	
169	/// The tracker write failed. The typed report SURVIVES here — evidence is
170	/// never lost to a tracker hiccup — beside the filing's own streams.
171	type Unfiled { report: InvestigationReport, filing_exit: Int, filing_stderr: String, session_id: String, teardown_ok: Bool }
172	
173	worker investigate_ops
174	  /// Clone `repo_url` to `<workspace_root>/<workflow_id>/repo`. Refuses (as
175	  /// data) when the destination already exists. Implemented by this
176	  /// folder's worker document, served with `aion worker awl` on the
177	  /// investigation box.
178	  action clone(repo_url: String, workspace_root: String, workflow_id: String) -> CloneProbe
179	    timeout 15m, retry 2 every 30s
180	  /// Read `<tree>/.investigation/report.json` back into the declared type.
181	  action read_report(workspace_root: String, workflow_id: String) -> ReportProbe
182	    timeout 5m, retry 2 every 30s
183	  /// Render the report mechanically and comment it onto the issue. The
184	  /// agent's prose never reaches the tracker except through the report
185	  /// schema; the comment leads with the read-by-hand law.
186	  action file_report(workspace_root: String, workflow_id: String, repo: String, number: String, session_id: String, control_reply: String) -> FilingProbe
187	    timeout 5m, retry 3 backoff 30s..5m
188	  /// Remove the run's tree, refusing any path outside the run root.
189	  action teardown(workspace_root: String, workflow_id: String) -> TeardownProbe
190	    timeout 5m, retry 2 every 30s
191	
192	worker investigator
193	  /// The investigation seat: a norn-backed agent worker started from this
194	  /// document with `aion worker agent`, dialing the estate server over
195	  /// liminal. `--workspace-root` confines norn to the run's own tree (the
196	  /// adapter expands `{workflow_id}` per dispatch); `cwd from repo` puts
197	  /// the session in the clone the mechanical legs provisioned. There is no
198	  /// sandbox beyond that — this runs under the box's own credentials, a
199	  /// standing risk accepted at the operator's explicit word (design paper
200	  /// §6.3).

201	  harness
202	    kind norn
203	    concurrency 1
204	    reconnect_initial_backoff 1s
205	    reconnect_max_backoff 30s
206	    reconnect_max_attempts 100
207	    env_pass "PATH", "HOME", "USER", "LOGNAME"
208	    args "--workspace-root", "/home/aion/fleet/runs/{workflow_id}", "--account", "default"
209	    cwd from repo
210	  /// The control seat: quote a literal at a known path, nothing else.
211	  action probe(repo: String, prompt: String) -> Reply
212	    agent, timeout 10m, retry 3 backoff 30s..5m
213	  /// The investigation itself. The prompt is complete and self-contained:
214	  /// the issue, the threshold that fired, the report path to write, and the
215	  /// schema to write it in — the session sees nothing but this string and
216	  /// the tree.
217	  action investigate(repo: String, prompt: String) -> Reply
218	    agent, timeout 90m, retry 2 backoff 1m..10m
219	
220	/// v1 serves the GitHub tracker only; any other tracker is refused by name
221	/// before anything is provisioned.
222	step admit
223	  outcome github: when issue.tracker == "github", route provision
224	  outcome other: otherwise,
225	    route unsupported_tracker(tracker: issue.tracker,
226	      reason: "v1 files and reads through gh; an IssueRef naming any other tracker is refused by name, never silently skipped")
227	
228	/// Provision the run's own tree. A refusal — including a leftover tree from
229	/// a collided dispatch — routes with its reason; nothing is deleted to make
230	/// room.
231	step provision
232	  clone(repo_url: repo_url, workspace_root: workspace_root, workflow_id: workflow.id) -> cloned
233	  outcome ok: when cloned.ok, route prove
234	  outcome refused: otherwise, route unprovisioned(refusal: cloned.refusal, node: node_label)
235	
236	/// Prove the pipeline against the CLONED tree before spending judgement: a
237	/// judge that cannot read the tree or follow an exact-reply instruction
238	/// produces confident verdicts indistinguishable from real ones.
239	step prove
240	  probe(repo: cloned.path, prompt: control_prompt) -> control
241	  outcome proven: when control.text == control_expect, route investigation
242	  outcome broken: otherwise, route teardown_unmeasured
243	
244	step investigation
245	  investigate(repo: cloned.path, prompt: investigate_prompt) -> reply
246	  outcome answered: when reply.stop_reason == "end_turn", route harvest
247	  outcome broken: otherwise, route teardown_unanswered
248	
249	/// The reply is a claim; the tree is the fact. Read the deliverable back
250	/// into the declared type and route on what the tree actually carries.
251	step harvest
252	  read_report(workspace_root: workspace_root, workflow_id: workflow.id) -> probe_result
253	  outcome present: when probe_result.report is present, route file_it
254	  outcome absent: otherwise, route teardown_unreported
255	
256	step file_it
257	  file_report(workspace_root: workspace_root, workflow_id: workflow.id,
258	    repo: issue.repo, number: issue.number,
259	    session_id: reply.session_id, control_reply: control.text) -> filing
260	  outcome ok: when filing.ok, route teardown_filed
261	  outcome red: otherwise, route teardown_unfiled
262	
263	/// Teardown is reached from every route that owns a tree; its receipt
264	/// travels in the payload. The re-proof guards on `probe_result.report` are
265	/// demanded by narrowing scope (a proof never escapes its arm), and their
266	/// impossible arms route honestly rather than pretending totality.
267	step teardown_filed
268	  teardown(workspace_root: workspace_root, workflow_id: workflow.id) -> cleaned
269	  outcome done: when probe_result.report is present,
270	    route filed(report: probe_result.report, filing_url: filing.url,
271	      session_id: reply.session_id, control_reply: control.text, teardown_ok: cleaned.ok)

225	## 4. Design decisions, each ruled here so the builder does not re-open them
226	
227	### 4.1 The documents
228	
229	New folder `workflows/repo-battery/`, per `workflows/README.md:45` ("Each directory carries its own
230	README with the inputs it takes"):
231	
232	| Path | What |
233	|---|---|
234	| `workflows/repo-battery/repo_battery.awl` | the workflow document — **ruled name `repo_battery`** |
235	| `workflows/repo-battery/repo_battery_worker.awl` | the worker document — **ruled queue `lane_repo_battery`** |
236	| `workflows/repo-battery/bin/*.sh` | the operation scripts (§4.2) |
237	| `workflows/repo-battery/README.md` | inputs, how to run, what a green does not prove |
238	| `workflows/repo-battery/proofs/` | phase-3 fixtures, harness, and receipts |
239	
240	**No edit to `workflows/gate/gate.awl`, `workflows/gates/gates.awl`, or
241	`workflows/gates/repo_gates.awl`.** All three verified present and untouched at this tree. v1 stays
242	in service; F3 (`workflows/gates/README.md:300-311`) governs cut-over per repo, in a later lane.
243	
244	### 4.2 Worker document + committed scripts — RULED, with its reason
245	
246	**Ruling: the mechanical logic lives in committed scripts under `workflows/repo-battery/bin/`,
247	invoked by the worker document's bodies.** Not an SDK crate (Vesper's ruling: a crate brings a
248	`Cargo.lock` that rots — sixteen out-of-workspace worker projects pinning beamr 0.6.1 through 0.18.2
249	while the root moved to 0.19.3). Not 400-character single-quoted `sh -c` bodies carrying python
250	either.
251	
252	The reason is a language constraint, not taste, and the repo states it:
253	`workflows/investigate/investigate_worker.awl:7-13` — *"worker-document run bodies admit no shell
254	variables (an AWL parameter is the only `$name` allowed), so any logic beyond one command lives in a
255	script file"*. `investigate_ops` is a live first-party workflow built exactly this way.
256	
257	Three things make this consistent with Vesper's "the ONE command stays reviewable text at a sha":
258	
259	1. A committed script **is** reviewable text at a sha, and its sha256 is witnessed into the receipt.
260	2. The whole-cloth / no-runtime-path law is `gate.awl`'s closed vocabulary (`gate.awl:8-15`), which
261	   this work is explicitly forbidden to edit and does not inherit.
262	3. This workflow *already* resolves a path at run time by design — the provisioned tree's own
263	   `scripts/battery.sh`. That is the reconciliation Vesper accepted and Artemis discharged. A rule
264	   the design has deliberately set aside at its centre cannot be reimposed at its edge.
265	
266	**Named for the landing desk as a planner's call**, so it is reviewed rather than assumed.
267	
268	### 4.3 The census is ONE activity, and that is deliberate
269	
270	L6 proves the workflow *could* iterate `legs_declared` with `sequence`. It must not. The declaration
271	is read **once**, in one script, at one site: `bin/census-declaration.sh`.
272	
273	Reason, and it is R3's: the selector-perturbation arm needs a **single nameable selector site** to
274	perturb. A selector smeared across a worker body, a workflow pipe chain and a step guard has three
275	places to be right and no address to break. One site, one `file:line`, one arm that can aim at it.
276	
277	The battery does not need iteration anyway: `scripts/battery.sh` runs the whole declared list itself
278	(`:226-239`) and reports per-leg rc in its manifest (`:264-274`). The workflow's job is to invoke,
279	census, witness and report — never to re-run a list.
280	
281	### 4.4 The flow
282	
283	`admit` → `provision` → `precheck` → `battery` → `verify` → `receipt` → `teardown`.
284	
285	- **`admit`** — input validation, before anything is provisioned: a waiver missing its author is
286	  refused here (`waivers |> any(.ruled_by == "")`, L7). Costs nothing; provisions nothing.
287	- **`provision`** — clone/worktree the subject repo at the caller-named ref into a **run-owned tree**
288	  under the venue's workspace root, never a person's checkout. Refusals are data, and a leftover
289	  destination refuses rather than being deleted — `workflows/investigate/bin/clone.sh:26` is the
290	  precedent, verbatim in register.
291	- **`precheck`** — venue pre-checks **recorded, not assumed**: toolchain pin vs venue toolchain (with
292	  targets), PATH order (rustup shim first), hydration state (G5: a declared refusal, **never an
293	  auto-install** — an instrument must not mutate the venue it measures), and the per-leg declared
294	  environment confirmed **by value** (§4.6).
295	- **`battery`** — ONE whole-cloth command: run **the tree's own** `scripts/battery.sh`,
296	  exit-zero-always, rc + log path + contended flag as data — the `gate_worker.awl:13-24` probe shape.
297	  **No retry** (L2).
298	- **`verify`** — run **the tree's own** `scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh` against the battery
299	  log. Its refusal IS the scope instrument (S3). Never reimplemented; the workflow holds no list.
300	- **`receipt`** — the terminal typed report (§5).
301	- **`teardown`** — run-owned tree only, root-guarded in the same script that does the `rm`, never a
302	  separate command: `workflows/investigate/bin/teardown.sh:3-6,14-28`. Teardown obligations are
303	  **surfaced, not assumed**, on every route that owns a tree.
304	
305	**No child workflows anywhere** — the cancellation contract abandons children. Every long leg under
306	process-group containment; a cancelled leg reports **CANCELLED MEASUREMENT**, never a result.
307	**The workflow timeout is the one duration**; no per-leg retry ladder.
308	
309	### 4.5 The absolute-path admission rule, stated precisely
310	
311	Refuse at admission a declared leg whose **command** contains a **literal absolute path** — a `/`
312	beginning a path token, not preceded by a word character or `$`. Keyed on the **path inside the
313	command**, never on the leg's name (§10.2: ten of thirteen estate gate lists carry such a leg under
314	differing names).
315	
316	**A variable-rooted path is NOT an absolute path.** `"$ABLATIVE_ESTATE_ROOT/tools/…"` is a declared-
317	environment leg (aion's own leg 23) and is handled by the environment pre-check, not by this rule.
318	Measured (§S5): a rule that reds it would red aion's honest declaration on its first real run, which
319	is how a correct instrument gets switched off.
320	
321	### 4.6 The environment pre-check, at Artemis's strength
322	
323	Not "confirmed set". For each name in a leg's declared `environment` block: **confirm and record the
324	VALUE** for non-secret variables; **presence plus a digest** for anything secret-shaped. The reason
325	is the correction's own: a variable set to a *different* value than the leg's scope assumes is the
326	silent scope change itself, and it passes a set-check. The effective environment is **recorded in
327	the receipt beside the frozen HEAD**, because receipts whose environments do not travel with their
328	verdicts are not comparable — pass counts compare verdicts, not what was asked.
329	
330	Standing true receipt for the class, carried into the field docs: a leg whose tests read a
331	`*_TEST_URL`-style variable and skip when unset measures a **different scope** with and without it,
332	while reporting the same green.
333	
334	---
335	
336	## 5. The receipt — R4 at full strength, now
337	
338	The terminal payload's fields are declared in **exactly this order**, and the order is load-bearing
339	(L8: declaration order is the serialization order, every run):
340	
341	1. `subject_repo` · 2. `ref_requested` · 3. `head_commit` · 4. `tree_path` ·
342	5. `gates_json_sha256` · 6. `battery_sha256` · 7. `script_witnesses` (`[ScriptWitness]`, sorted by
343	`path`) · 8. `venue` · 9. `environment` (`[EnvRecord]`, in declaration order per leg) ·
344	10. `legs_declared` · 11. `legs_executed` · 12. `legs` (`[LegRecord]`: name, rc, status) ·
345	13. `verify_verdict` · 14. `waivers` · 15. `verdict`.
346	
347	**R4, verbatim and binding: this stable-shape-and-order requirement is LOAD-BEARING NOW, at full
348	strength, even though the drift check that consumes it is out of scope. Comparability cannot be
349	retrofitted onto receipts already written, so this phase ships witnesses to the ordering discipline
350	on the strength of a consumer that does not exist yet. A builder must not read "drift check out of
351	scope" as licence to drop the ordering.**
352	
353	**Vocabulary, binding everywhere shas are described — in this plan, in both documents, in the field
354	docs, in the README, in the reports: witness / record / attest. NEVER seal, NEVER pin.** A seal
355	REFUSES on mismatch; this records the sha256 and proceeds — it tells you afterwards which bytes ran.
356	And it cannot be a seal: the instrument lives inside the tree it measures, so there is no sha the
357	operator can pin the subject repo against that the subject repo cannot also change. Pinning an
358	expected sha in the operator's document is the two-lists problem wearing a different hat. Trust sits
359	where it actually sits: the subject repo's review and its landing gate.
360	*(Note: `gate_worker.awl:1-6` and `investigate_worker.awl:13` say "sealed" — pre-existing text,
361	not this work's to edit and not this work's precedent.)*
362	
363	### The three sentences that must appear in the receipt type's own field docs
364	
365	Not in the `//!` header. In the **field documentation**, which L1 proves is a first-class AWL
366	construct and which the beam sidecar carries as JSON-Schema `description` (§1.2) — because the
367	reader who tidies this away will be holding the field docs, not the design paper.
368	
369	- **G2 — verdict inversion, on `verdict`.** A red gate routes to workflow SUCCESS; `Failed` is
370	  reserved for could-not-measure; only `unproven` routes to failure. *With its reason:* the status
371	  answers "did I measure?", the receipt answers "what did I measure?" — and a red gate reporting
372	  SUCCESS is exactly the shape a later reader tidies away.
373	- **R1 — the authority sentence, on the fields that name a ref and a venue.** "No new trust" is true
374	  of the CODE and false of the VENUE: pre-existing, the self-gating hazard sat inside aion's own CI
375	  under aion's authority; this workflow moves it to a fleet venue that may hold credentials, network
376	  reach, and neighbours. Stated plainly: **A BATTERY RUNS WITH THE VENUE'S AUTHORITY, AND NAMING A
377	  REF IS THEREFORE AN AUTHORITY-BEARING ACT.**
378	- **R2 — `undeclared`'s explicit status, in the same field docs.** Workflow status **SUCCESS** (the
379	  workflow measured the tree and found no contract — a determinate census result, not a
380	  could-not-measure); receipt verdict the typed literal **`undeclared`**, which consumers **MUST**
381	  treat as **not-a-verdict**: never green, never red, never pass-by-omission. A refusal with no
382	  assigned status resolves to the runtime's default, and a repo with no `gates.json` must never be
383	  able to read as a pass.
384	
385	Plus **R3**: `legs_declared` resolving to zero legs → **typed refusal naming the selector path**, no
386	verdict. A census returns empty when its selector is dead, and that is byte-identical to the thing
387	being absent; zero legs is a value that would compare, render, and pass proofs intact (S4 measured
388	this at the instrument level).
389	
390	And: a declared leg that did not run → **`unproven`** — not red, not green. Waivers are per-run, each
391	naming leg + reason + who ruled it; a green-with-waivers receipt lists its waived legs, because the
392	denominator travels beside the verdict.
393	
394	**`legs_declared` comes from the provisioned tree's `gates.json`, NEVER from the venue.** Proof 8
395	sits on this invariant's path.
396	
397	---
398	
399	## 6. Requirement → phase map, with the venue split
400	
401	Phases are sequential. Nothing in phase 3 starts before phase 2 lands.
402	
403	### Phase 1 — the workflow: provision, invoke, receipt
404

  exit 0

tree=$1

venue=$(hostname)
refusal=""
toolchain="not-declared"
targets='[]'

if [[ -f "$tree/rust-toolchain.toml" ]]; then
  toolchain=$(awk -F'"' '/^[[:space:]]*channel[[:space:]]*=/{print $2; exit}' "$tree/rust-toolchain.toml")
  mapfile -t declared_targets < <(awk '
    /^[[:space:]]*targets[[:space:]]*=/ { inside=1 }
    inside { while (match($0, /"[^"]+"/)) { print substr($0, RSTART+1, RLENGTH-2); $0=substr($0, RSTART+RLENGTH) } }
    inside && /]/ { exit }
  ' "$tree/rust-toolchain.toml")
  targets=$(printf '%s\n' "${declared_targets[@]:-}" | jq -Rsc 'split("\n") | map(select(length > 0))')
  actual=$(rustc --version | awk '{print $2}')
  if [[ -n "$toolchain" && "$actual" != "$toolchain" ]]; then
    refusal="rust toolchain mismatch: tree requests $toolchain but venue rustc is $actual"
  fi
  cargo_path=$(command -v cargo || true)
  case "$cargo_path" in
    "$HOME/.cargo/bin/"*) ;;
    *)
      if [[ -z "$refusal" ]]; then
        refusal="PATH order refusal: rustup cargo shim is not first (resolved $cargo_path)"
      fi
      ;;
  esac
  while IFS= read -r target; do
    if ! rustup target list --installed --toolchain "$toolchain" | grep -Fxq "$target"; then
      if [[ -z "$refusal" ]]; then
        refusal="rust target missing for $toolchain: $target"
      fi
    fi
  done < <(jq -r '.[]' <<<"$targets")
fi

if [[ -f "$tree/bun.lock" || -f "$tree/bun.lockb" ]]; then
  if [[ ! -d "$tree/node_modules" && -z "$refusal" ]]; then
    refusal="hydration refusal: repository documents bun dependencies but node_modules is absent; run bun install --frozen-lockfile outside the measurement"
  fi
fi

environment='[]'
while IFS= read -r name; do
  [[ -n "$name" ]] || continue
  if [[ -v "$name" ]]; then
    value=${!name}
    if secret_shaped "$name"; then
      digest=$(printf '%s' "$value" | sha256sum | awk '{print $1}')
      record=$(jq -cn --arg name "$name" --arg digest "$digest" \
        '{name:$name, present:true, secret:true, value:"", digest:$digest}')
    else
      record=$(jq -cn --arg name "$name" --arg value "$value" \
        '{name:$name, present:true, secret:false, value:$value, digest:""}')
    fi
  else
    record=$(jq -cn --arg name "$name" \

    if [[ -z "$refusal" ]]; then
      refusal="declared environment variable is absent: $name"

  fi

done < <(jq -r '[.legs[] | (.environment // [])[]] | unique[]' "$tree/gates.json")

script_witnesses='[]'
while IFS= read -r script; do
  path=${script#"$tree/"}

  witness=$(jq -cn --arg path "$path" --arg sha256 "$(sha256_file "$script")" '{path:$path, sha256:$sha256}')
  script_witnesses=$(jq -c --argjson witness "$witness" '. + [$witness]' <<<"$script_witnesses")

1	//! gate_ops — the measurement half of the gate workflow, WHOLE CLOTH: every
2	//! command is written out in full inside this document and sealed into the
3	//! package's content hash at deploy. No script files on any box, no path a
4	//! command resolves at run time, nothing on the operator's machine — the
5	//! review of this file is the review of exactly what will run (Tom's order,
6	//! 2026-08-18: "the commands need to be written up, whole cloth").
7	//!
8	//! Served with `aion worker awl` on a fleet box; the commands run on THAT
9	//! host. Each body is `sh -c '<the whole script>' -- <params>`: the script
10	//! text is literal to AWL (single-quote region), parameters arrive as sh
11	//! positionals, and a parameter value can never become code.
12	//!
13	//! EXIT ZERO ALWAYS, REFUSAL AS DATA: every anticipated face — red suite,
14	//! missing tree, unreadable log — returns exit-zero as a typed probe with
15	//! the rc or refusal named, because a nonzero exit is a retryable-then-
16	//! terminal activity failure and the workflow must ROUTE on these faces.
17	//!
18	//! CONTENTION CLASSIFIED AT THE SOURCE: each leg greps its OWN log for the
19	//! contention signatures measured on this estate (EMFILE "Too many open
20	//! files"; lld deaths as "LLVM ERROR", "signal: 11", "SIGSEGV"; haematite
21	//! shard-actor timeouts "timed out waiting for shard actor" — aion#54, load-
22	//! induced flake failing otherwise-green tests) and reports
23	//! `contended` beside the rc — the workflow's rerun policy consumes the
24	//! classification, it never invents one.
25	//!
26	//! ENVIRONMENT DECLARED, NOT INHERITED: the workflow gate context can carry
27	//! an EMPTY HOME (measured 2026-08-18, fleet-53 reds); every body sets PATH
28	//! absolutely, defaults HOME, and raises the fd soft limit inline. The PATH
29	//! names BOTH estate hosts' toolchains (box /home/aion, Mac /Users/tom) —
30	//! absolute, first-match-wins, one document honestly serving two venues
31	//! until the server and gates live on the box alone.
32	worker gate_ops
33	  /// Identify the tree: it must exist and be a git work tree; its HEAD pins
34	  /// every verdict to the exact tree measured.
35	  action probe_tree(tree: String) -> TreeProbe
36	    run json "sh -c 'set -u; PATH=/home/aion/.cargo/bin:/Users/tom/.cargo/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; export PATH; if [ -z \"${HOME:-}\" ]; then if [ -d /home/aion ]; then HOME=/home/aion; else HOME=/Users/tom; fi; export HOME; fi; t=\"$1\"; if [ ! -d \"$t\" ]; then printf \"{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"refusal\\\":\\\"tree directory does not exist\\\",\\\"head_commit\\\":\\\"\\\"}\"; exit 0; fi; h=$(git -C \"$t\" rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null); if [ -z \"$h\" ]; then printf \"{\\\"ok\\\":false,\\\"refusal\\\":\\\"not a git work tree or HEAD unreadable\\\",\\\"head_commit\\\":\\\"\\\"}\"; exit 0; fi; printf \"{\\\"ok\\\":true,\\\"refusal\\\":\\\"\\\",\\\"head_commit\\\":\\\"%s\\\"}\" \"$h\"' -- $tree"
37	  /// Full workspace test suite at bounded parallelism; log to the tree.
38	  action run_test_workspace(tree: String, kind: String, jobs: Int) -> LegProbe
39	    run json "sh -c 'set -u; PATH=/home/aion/.cargo/bin:/Users/tom/.cargo/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; export PATH; if [ -z \"${HOME:-}\" ]; then if [ -d /home/aion ]; then HOME=/home/aion; else HOME=/Users/tom; fi; export HOME; fi; ulimit -n 65536 2>/dev/null || true; t=\"$1\"; k=\"$2\"; j=\"$3\"; mkdir -p \"$t/.gate\" 2>/dev/null; l=\"$t/.gate/$k.log\"; ( cd \"$t\" && cargo test --workspace -j \"$j\" ) > \"$l\" 2>&1; rc=$?; g=false; [ \"$rc\" = \"0\" ] && g=true; c=false; grep -qE \"Too many open files|LLVM ERROR|signal: 11|SIGSEGV|timed out waiting for shard actor\" \"$l\" 2>/dev/null && c=true; printf \"{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\\\"green\\\":%s,\\\"rc\\\":%d,\\\"contended\\\":%s,\\\"log_path\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\\\"refusal\\\":\\\"\\\"}\" \"$k\" \"$g\" \"$rc\" \"$c\" \"$l\"' -- $tree $kind $jobs"
40	  /// Workspace clippy wall, all targets, warnings denied.
41	  action run_clippy_workspace(tree: String, kind: String, jobs: Int) -> LegProbe
42	    run json "sh -c 'set -u; PATH=/home/aion/.cargo/bin:/Users/tom/.cargo/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin; export PATH; if [ -z \"${HOME:-}\" ]; then if [ -d /home/aion ]; then HOME=/home/aion; else HOME=/Users/tom; fi; export HOME; fi; ulimit -n 65536 2>/dev/null || true; t=\"$1\"; k=\"$2\"; j=\"$3\"; mkdir -p \"$t/.gate\" 2>/dev/null; l=\"$t/.gate/$k.log\"; ( cd \"$t\" && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -j \"$j\" -- -D warnings ) > \"$l\" 2>&1; rc=$?; g=false; [ \"$rc\" = \"0\" ] && g=true; c=false; grep -qE \"Too many open files|LLVM ERROR|signal: 11|SIGSEGV|timed out waiting for shard actor\" \"$l\" 2>/dev/null && c=true; printf \"{\\\"kind\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\\\"green\\\":%s,\\\"rc\\\":%d,\\\"contended\\\":%s,\\\"log_path\\\":\\\"%s\\\",\\\"refusal\\\":\\\"\\\"}\" \"$k\" \"$g\" \"$rc\" \"$c\" \"$l\"' -- $tree $kind $jobs"

2	#
3	# Measures the claim `scripts/battery.sh` makes about itself: that the set of
4	# gates it EXECUTED is exactly the set `gates.json` DECLARES.
5	#
6	# WHY THIS IS NOT THE DRIFT-CHECKER THAT WAS REJECTED
7	#
8	# When aion's two gate lists were collapsed into one, a drift-checker comparing
9	# the two was refused on the grounds that it would be a THIRD copy of the same
10	# list — the cure for one truth in two places is subtraction, not a third party
11	# to referee the pair. That still holds, and this is a different instrument.
12	#
13	# It holds no list of its own. It reads the one declaration and compares it
14	# against what a run actually did. The battery's claim — "the two sets cannot
15	# differ by construction" — is exactly the kind of confident claim that stops
16	# people measuring, and construction arguments have been wrong here before: the
17	# same script argued a fixed population while `if require_tool gleam` was
18	# quietly shrinking it. So the claim gets an instrument.
19	#
20	# WHAT IT CHECKS
21	#
22	#   1. Every declared leg appears in the run.  A leg that vanished — skipped,
23	#      swallowed by a conditional, lost to a reader bug — is the original defect
24	#      returning, and a shrunken population reads as a clean tree.
25	#   2. Every executed leg was declared.  A leg the runner invents is a gate
26	#      nobody can find by reading the declaration.
27	#   3. The COUNTS match, not just the sets.  Two legs sharing a name collapse
28	#      into one set member, so a set comparison alone would call a declaration
29	#      with a duplicated name clean while one of the pair never ran.
30	#   4. The log carries EXACTLY ONE `EXECUTED_LEGS` line.  Two concatenated runs
31	#      in one file would otherwise be judged on whichever line was read first.
32	#
33	# WHAT IT CANNOT SEE — stated so the green is not read as more than it is.
34	# It compares NAMES. It does not know whether a leg's `cmd` ran the thing the
35	# leg is named after; a leg named `rust:clippy` whose command is `true` passes
36	# here. That is the paired-test/posture-control layer's job, not this one's.
37	#
38	# ITS OWN RED PATH IS RUNNABLE, and does not need a broken battery to show:
39	#
40	#   AION_BATTERY_SELF_TEST=1 scripts/battery.sh > /tmp/self.log 2>&1
41	#   scripts/gates/verify-declaration.sh /tmp/self.log     # MUST exit 1
42	#
43	# Self-test mode runs two synthetic legs and no declared one, so a verifier
